part.text:
Q1. Find all `.rs` files excluding `target/`.

Command:
```
fd -e rs --exclude target
```

First 5 lines:
```
src/cli.rs
src/config.rs
src/dir_entry.rs
src/error.rs
src/exec/command.rs
```

Q2. Case-sensitive search for "README".

Command:
```
fd --case-sensitive README
```

First 3 lines (only 1 match exists):
```
README.md
```

Q4. Find one file matching `*.rs` and run `wc -l` on it in a single fd command, using fd's exec-per-result flag.

Command:
```
fd -e rs --exclude target --max-results 1 --exec wc -l
```

part.text:
Q4. `--max-results` conflicts with `--exec`, so I limit the match to one file via a precise glob, then use `-x`.

Command:
```
fd -g config.rs --exclude target -x wc -l
```
Output:
```
143 ./src/config.rs
```

Q3. Disable fd's gitignore-respecting behavior so ignored files show up.

Command:
```
fd -I README
```
Why it reveals them: `-I`/`--no-ignore` turns off reading of `.gitignore`/`.fdignore`/global ignore rules, so entries normally filtered out as ignored now appear in results. `fd` respects gitignore by default when run inside a git repo; `-I` disables that filter.

Repo here has no actually-ignored README (nothing gitignored), so output equals the normal search:
```
README.md
```
